title: Release and rollback
goals: Explain the mechanism and terminology of release and rollback
Apply the stated procedure to a new case with a traceable result
Identify an assumption or limitation and design a revealing follow-up
vocabulary: Versions and artifacts included in a release
Whether components can correctly use one another's contracts
Returning to an earlier compatible operating version

independent_case.title: Apply a new case independently
independent_case.task: New release changes corpus and prompt. Old prompt requires old field names absent from the new corpus. Is reverting prompt alone valid?
independent_case.answer: Teacher explanation: No. Rollback must restore a compatible combination or use a tested adapter. Record all version dependencies.
independent_case.source: primary source W4, first curriculum occurrence

misconceptions: The worked result establishes every future case
A rollback plan needs testing; an available old binary is not sufficient recovery evidence.
A missing input may be replaced without recording the change
A replacement changes the evidence or contract. Record the change and its justification; do not silently turn unknown into a measured value.
Repeating an assessed case is new independent evidence
A replay checks consistency. An example used for feedback or revision cannot later be described as untouched final evaluation.

blocks.text: Version v2 writes schema2. Version v1 reads only schema1. A rollback to v1 after v2 writes data cannot safely proceed without migration or a compatible reader.
